claims.text: Aluminum pack cementation can improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed aluminum pack-cementation treatment is performed at 1000 °C for 2 hours.
Aluminum pack cementation of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr forms an Al2O3 scale.
The resulting Al2O3 scale is continuous and adherent.
The Al2O3 scale prevents oxygen ingress.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C without applied load, treated material will exhibit a 50% reduction in oxidation-induced mass gain relative to untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed protection is applicable in air from 600 to 1000 °C for exposure times of 1 to 10 hours under unloaded conditions.
The effectiveness of the Al2O3 scale may depend on the composition and microstructure of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a 50% reduction in mass gain, but the stated rule falsifies it only if treated material has more than a 20% increase relative to untreated material. Outcomes ranging from a 49% reduction through a 20% increase would fail the prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
